bib.title: CatBoost: unbiased boosting with categorical features

read.skipped: Appendix A proof algebra (Propositions 1-3, Lemmas 1-2) read only in part; text is garbled and the claim is stated in Theorem 1 in the body

question: Do existing gradient boosting implementations suffer a prediction shift from target leakage (in gradient estimation and in categorical target statistics), and does an ordering-principle fix improve accuracy?
hypothesis: Target leakage in target statistics and in residual estimation causes a shift of train vs test distributions; ordering (ordered TS and ordered boosting) removes it and improves quality, most on small datasets.
contributions: Identify and formally analyse prediction shift in gradient boosting (Theorem 1)
Ordered boosting, a permutation-driven alternative to classic gradient boosting
Ordered target statistics for categorical features
CatBoost library combining them, compared with XGBoost and LightGBM

method.summary: CatBoost builds oblivious decision trees by gradient boosting, with categorical features turned into ordered target statistics computed over random permutations and, in Ordered mode, gradients for each example computed from supporting models that never saw it. It is compared with XGBoost and LightGBM on 9 binary classification datasets, and ablated over boosting mode, TS type, feature combinations and number of permutations.

training.optimizer: gradient boosting with decision trees; leaf values by gradient step
training.lr: tuned: log-uniform [e^-7, 1] for all three libraries
training.steps: number of trees chosen by search over [1, 5000], minimum 5-fold-averaged logloss
training.regularisation: CatBoost l2_leaf_reg log-uniform [1,10], random_strength {1,20}, bagging_temperature uniform [0,1]; Bayesian bootstrap subsampling
training.hardware: Intel Xeon E3-12xx 2.6GHz, 16 cores, 64GB RAM, 16 threads (timing test only)
training.wall_clock: time per tree on Epsilon: CatBoost Plain 1.1 s, Ordered 1.9 s, XGBoost 3.9 s, LightGBM 1.1 s

other.tuning: 50 steps of Hyperopt TPE (tpe.suggest) minimising logloss, 5-fold CV stratified on the 80% train part
other.xgboost search space: eta logU[e^-7,1]; max_depth U{2..10}; subsample U[0.5,1]; colsample_bytree U[0.5,1]; colsample_bylevel U[0.5,1]; min_child_weight logU[e^-16,e^5]; alpha, lambda, gamma 0.5*0 + 0.5*logU[e^-16,e^2]
other.lightgbm search space: learning_rate logU[e^-7,1]; num_leaves discrete logU[1,e^7]; feature_fraction U[0.5,1]; bagging_fraction U[0.5,1]; min_sum_hessian_in_leaf logU[e^-16,e^5]; min_data_in_leaf discrete logU[1,e^6]; lambda_l1, lambda_l2 mixed as above
other.catboost search space: learning_rate logU[e^-7,1]; random_strength {1,20}; one_hot_max_size {0,25}; l2_leaf_reg logU[1,10]; bagging_temperature U[0,1]; gradient_iterations {1,10}
other.timing test: learning rate set so that overfitting starts near 7000 trees; mean time to train 8000 trees; no feature subsampling or bagging
other.Epsilon: default parameters, only tree count tuned
other.permutations: s+1 independent permutations; sigma_1..sigma_s for tree structure, sigma_0 for leaf values; s value used in main experiments not stated (Fig 4 varies s 1..10)
other.TS prior: Equation 4 smoothing a>0, p = average target; value of a not stated

inference.samples: one random 80/20 split per dataset; no repeated seeds stated

other.test-time TS: computed on the whole training data

metrics.name: logloss
metrics.definition: binary log loss on the 20% test set; baselines reported as relative increase over CatBoost

eval.protocol: Single 80/20 split per dataset; paired one-tailed t-test for significance (p much less than 0.01 except Appetency, Churn, Upselling); what the test pairs over is not stated

limits: Prediction shift is proved only for a toy regression (quadratic loss, 2 binary features, 2 stumps); general case is argued, not proved.
All comparisons use one random 80/20 split per dataset; no seed repeats or confidence intervals beyond a paired t-test whose pairing is unstated.
Only binary classification; metrics are logloss and zero-one loss, no AUC.
Authors tuned baselines with 50 TPE steps but Epsilon used defaults for all libraries.
Only CatBoost gets feature combinations, so the headline gap mixes ordered boosting, combinations and oblivious trees; the raw setting shows the base GBDT is on par.
Ordered mode is about 1.7 times slower than Plain on Epsilon.
Library versions are from 2017-2018 (catboost 0.3, xgboost 0.6, lightgbm 0.1).
GPU timings are deferred to a GitHub page.
Footer reads 'Preprint. Work in progress.'; this arXiv v5 PDF prints no venue.

terms.definition: the distribution of F(x_k) | x_k for a training example is shifted from that of F(x) | x for a test example, caused by gradients using the targets of the same data the model was built on
target statistic for example k computed over D_k = {x_j : sigma(j) < sigma(k)} for a random permutation sigma, and over all of D for test examples
boosting where the residual for example j comes from a supporting model M_{j-1} trained only on the first j-1 examples of a permutation
the same splitting criterion is used across an entire level of the tree
